content.text: Check pulse & RR Q 5 - 10s  -if unsure about pulse, start compressions
F PT FOUND & SUS HYPOXIA CAN DO 2MIN CPR B4 EMERGENCY RESPONSE
Agonal Gasps = w/in few min of arrest -snort/snore/groan -BEGIN CPR IMMEDIATELY.
Open mouth, jaw/neck/head move w gasps. Forceful or weak. Slow irregular rate
Compression rate: 100 - 120/min. Depth 2 - 2.4in (5 - 6cm) -> allow complete recoil of chest b/n compression. Ventilation: over 1s, enough for visible rise.
Maximum interruption time for chest compressions is 10s.
CCF: Chest compression fraction = total time spent performing chest compressions.
Minimally, CCF should be 60%.  Ideally CCF should be 80 %
pads in anterolateral placement w jewelry piercing on pt @navel: move pads ±1in from piercing
immediately following a shock: CPR (start w compressions)
faint pulse after checking for 5-10s -> rescue breathing
Coronary perfusion pressure (CPP): aortic relaxation (diastolic) - art atrial relaxation (diastolic)
correlates w myocardial blood flow & ROSC (return of spont circulation)
ROSC only if Partial P end-tidal CO2 (PETCO2) ±10mmHg - b/c related to CO
initial assessment: visualization & scene safety -b4 approach
BLS assessment: only in unconscious pt
No pulse: CPR -> ‘push hard & fast’ -> check rhythm/shock -> repeat Q2min -> primary assessment
Pulse, no breathing: 1breath/6s -> primary assessment -> check pulse Q2min.
Maintain open airway: head tilt-chin lift, OPA, NPA
Advanced airway: is advanced airway indicated? Is so, confirm placement of airway device and secure
Can defer until: ⍉respond to initial CPR/defib or until ROSC
Laryngeal airmasks, laryngeal tube can be placed during chest compressions
breathing: vent/breathing adequate? -monitor quantitative waveform capnography & oxyHgb sat
excessive air prevent ♡ from getting enough blood flow -> ↓blood return to ♡, ↓CO, ↓coronary perfusion P
↑gastric inflation  via speed & P of air -> vomiting -> stomach content aspiration
Monitor CPR quality (Effective compressions): Quantitative waveform capnography
Indirect measurement of CO during chest compressions b/c amount of CO2 exhaled =assoc w amount of blood passing lungs
PETCO2 ±10mmHg -> contin = as ↑as poss in quality CPR
Cardiac rhythm: defib or cardioversion indicated?
Cardioversion= AFib, AFlutter, SVT, VT, WPW syndrome
⍉ if sinus tachy, digoxin toxicity induced arrythmia, sus clot (if ⍉new onset AFib)
ROSC present? Is pt w pulse unstable?
Quickly: responsiveness, level of consciousness, pupil dilation
Obvious trauma signs, bleeding, burns, unusual marking
Secondary assessment: DDx -> focused Hx & tx underlying
Sx/S: Breathing difficulty,↑HR/RR, febrile/HA, abd pain, bleeding
Allergies: meds, foods, latex & assoc rxn
Meds: Rx, OTC, herbs, supplements, vitamins, inhalers
Last Meal: time & nature or liquid & food
US can help Dx, monitor response to interventions
Recognize hypovolemia: initial = sinus tachy, ↑w diastolic, ↓w systolic P -> contin ↓blood vol -> ↓BP -> undetectable BUT narrow QRS & ↑rate contin (PEA)
Tx: IVF, compression,  ventilation, other ALS interventions
